source_claims.statement: UAF in TLS shutdown (tls_close frees xfer_buffer) while nested BDAT ungetc continues to write into freed memory.
Human struggled with heap grooming due to unfreed GnuTLS structures and store_reset; initial LLM produced glibc largebin/FSOP style; pivoted to Exim custom store allocator.
Autonomous system succeeded on non-ASLR and ASLR-no-PIE stages but failed production ASLR+PIE; human+LLM achieved stack leak on production target.

research_questions.formulation: Does the interaction between TLS shutdown and BDAT chunking produce a usable memory corruption in Exim's receive path?

unobserved_history: Full intermediate agent traces for both human-assisted and autonomous runs
Exact negative test results that led to abandoning largebin approach
forbidden_inferences: Do not equate autonomous system's failure on production build with falsification of the UAF hypothesis
Parallel human and autonomous runs are distinct; do not merge into one serial diary
next_evidence_actions: Note two parallel research runs (human+LLM vs fully autonomous)
